assessments.reasoning: Section 1.1.1 on printed p. 299 specifies parallel evaluation for comma conjunction and limits evaluation of the second ampersand conjunct to successful termination of the first. Program 1 on pp. 300-301 uses the two forms for background and foreground calls respectively.

challenge.method: Compared success, failure, and waiting of the first conjunct, the Program 1 foreground and background branches, the Program 2 output discussion, and the separate sequential clause-search punctuation.
challenge.results: The evaluation dependency requires success, so failure and suspended execution do not unlock the second conjunct. Printed p. 301 contrasts withholding output in a guard with the sequential conjunction's ability to delay its second conjunct while exposing output of the first. Clause search uses a different operator.

limitations: The reviewed semantics concerns evaluation dependency, with no claim of actual simultaneous execution or output buffering by ampersand.
